title: confiture verify-checksums --format json
description: File-integrity verification of applied migrations: SHA-256 of each migration file compared against the checksum stored when it was applied. Detects files modified after application. Distinct from `migrate verify`, which checks runtime state via .verify.sql sidecars. Added in 0.39.0 (#189). Consumers read ok and issues[]. ok is true only when a comparison actually happened and found nothing (ledger_present && summary.mismatched == 0); see ok and was_skipped for why those are two conditions rather than one (#311). Exit code is 1 when mismatches are found — a success-signal, not an error — so a crash (config/DB error, or an absent ledger without --allow-uninitialized) emits the error envelope (error-envelope.schema.json) instead of this shape. NOT part of the fraisier adapter contract.

ok.description: True when a comparison happened and found no mismatch: ledger_present && summary.mismatched == 0. Until 1.12.0 this was computed as summary.mismatched == 0 alone, and an absent ledger produces no mismatches — so a run under --allow-uninitialized that compared zero files reported ok true, and a consumer following this schema read green from a run that did no work (#311). ok and the exit code answer different questions: the exit code answers "should this gate trip" (and --allow-uninitialized is the operator declaring in advance that a ledger-less database must not trip it), while ok answers "did verification succeed" — which it did not, because it did not happen. So ok false at exit 0 is the coherent pairing, not a contradiction.

was_skipped.description: True when the run verified nothing because the ledger was absent — only reachable under --allow-uninitialized, since otherwise an absent ledger raises PRECON_1001. Always present, never absent-on-success: a key that appears on one path only makes every consumer branch before it can read it. A consumer that wants "clean" and "skipped" to read differently branches on this; one that only wants "is it safe to ship" needs ok alone (1.12.0, #311).

ledger_present.description: Whether the migration ledger table (tracking_table, default tb_confiture) exists. False is only emitted under --allow-uninitialized; without that flag an absent ledger raises PRECON_1001 (exit 2) with the error envelope. Distinct from a present-but-empty ledger, which reports true with summary.checked 0. Spelled ledger_present, not tb_confiture_present, because the table name is configurable (#190). When false, was_skipped is true and ok is false — read was_skipped for the outcome rather than inferring it from this field.

fixed.description: Number of stored checksums rewritten to match the current files. Present only when --fix was passed.

checked.description: Applied migrations whose checksums were compared. 0 when the ledger is absent.

mismatched.description: Applied migrations whose file no longer matches its stored checksum.

tracking_table.description: The ledger name as configured — the project's tracking_table, not necessarily the tb_confiture default. May be bare or schema-qualified; see resolved_table for what it actually resolved to.

resolved_table.description: The schema-qualified relation the ledger name resolved to for this session, e.g. "public.tb_confiture" (0.41.0, #188). A bare tracking_table resolves through search_path, so this is how a consumer learns which of several same-named tables was actually read. Null when the ledger did not resolve — only emitted so under --allow-uninitialized, since otherwise an absent ledger raises PRECON_1001.

issues.description: One entry per checksum mismatch, using the shared issue object. Empty on a clean run.

parser.description: What parsed the SQL behind this payload (0.50.0): the installed pglast release and the PostgreSQL grammar major it embeds.
